label: input "v" fed back early in the copy phase (v was the 1st or 2nd original token)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase when the token being fed back in is "v". In practice that means v was one of the first original tokens: 99.9% of activation mass has in_tok == v. It is strongest at recall_idx 1 (input v right after <DEL>, i.e. first_tok == v; 81% of mass and all top examples, reaching about 5.4). It is weaker at recall_idx 2 (orig(1) == v; 18% of mass, about 0.3-0.5 of max) and fires only on short sequences there (L <= 6). It barely fires at recall_idx 3 and never later. Magnitude falls as L and t grow; a v fed back late in long sequences does not fire. It never fires on v in the original phase or at the delimiter, and almost never on other tokens (a few weak h/j cases). The output token has little effect.

issues: The predicate has a systematic false-positive class: recall_idx==1 with long sequences. With in_tok==v at recall_idx 1, L==9 fires only 8.3% of the time (2718 predicted, test), and L==8 fires 71%. Taken together, L>=8 has precision 0.39 on dev. So 'first_tok==v fires' is not unconditional. The length cutoff that the predicate applies to recall_idx 2 (L<=6) also exists for recall_idx 1 (L<=8). The explanation only gestures at this ('magnitude falls as L and t grow').
Consistent with this, the t-profile shows the feature never fires at t>=12 and almost never at t>=10. That fits a joint cutoff on recall_idx and L (roughly t<=9), not a cutoff on recall_idx alone.

These claims check out: copy phase only (2 activations outside it); 99.9% of activation mass has in_tok==v; recall_idx 1 holds 81% of mass and recall_idx 2 holds 18%; recall_idx 3 is tiny (0.5% of mass) and zero after that; recall_idx 2 with L<=6 has precision 0.95, while L==7 has precision 0.17; a few weak h/j activations.
The remaining misses after the fix are scattered tiny activations (around 0.0-0.06 of max), mostly v at recall_idx 2 for L=7, or recall_idx 3 for short L. That is noise.
skeptic.revised_label: input "v" fed back as the 1st copy-phase input (L<=8) or the 2nd (L<=6); dies off in long sequences
